content.query:
// KPI drill-down. Driven by {SelectedKpi}, which the tile row exports on click.
//
// Every branch returns the SAME shape -- Segment / Detail / Count / Note -- so a
// single grid can render any of them. The alternative (one panel per KPI, six
// conditional visibilities) is six times the surface area for the same result.
//
// The branches are filtered on a let-bound scalar rather than assembled with
// string concatenation, so the query is statically analysable and every branch
// is validated at bind time even when it is not the selected one.
let Sel = "{SelectedKpi}";
let Ident = materialize(
    IdentityInfo
    | project TimeGenerated, AccountObjectId, AccountUPN, Department,
              IsAccountEnabled, UserType, AssignedRoles, JobTitle
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by AccountObjectId
    | extend Department = iif(isempty(Department), "Unmapped", Department)
    | where "{DeptFilter}" == "*" or Department == "{DeptFilter}");
let InScope = Ident | project Principal = tolower(AccountUPN);
let Scoped  = "{DeptFilter}" != "*";
//
let B_Total =
    Ident
    | where Sel == "Total employees"
    | summarize Count = dcount(AccountObjectId) by Segment = Department
    | extend Detail = "Employees in division",
             Note   = "Counts Member and untyped identities. Guests excluded from the headline tile.";
//
let B_Enabled =
    Ident
    | where Sel == "Enabled accounts"
    | extend State = case(IsAccountEnabled == true, "Enabled",
                          IsAccountEnabled == false, "Disabled or dormant",
                                                     "Unknown state")
    | summarize Count = dcount(AccountObjectId) by Segment = Department, State
    | extend Detail = State,
             Note   = "Disabled accounts that still hold roles or recent activity are worth a look.";
//
let B_Priv =
    Ident
    | where Sel == "Privileged identities"
    | extend RoleCount = array_length(todynamic(AssignedRoles))
    | where RoleCount > 0
    | extend Tier = case(RoleCount >= 5, "5+ roles",
                         RoleCount >= 3, "3-4 roles",
                         RoleCount == 2, "2 roles",
                                         "1 role")
    | summarize Count = dcount(AccountObjectId) by Segment = Department, Tier
    | extend Detail = Tier,
             Note   = "Directory role count is the blast-radius input to the risk index.";
//
let B_Risk =
    union isfuzzy=true
      (BehaviorAnalytics
       | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where InvestigationPriority > 0
       | extend P = tolower(coalesce(iif(isempty(UserPrincipalName), '', UserPrincipalName),
                                     iif(isempty(ActorPrincipalName), '', ActorPrincipalName),
                                     iif(isempty(UserName), '', UserName)))
       | where isnotempty(P) | where not(Scoped) or P in (InScope)
       | distinct P | extend Source = "UEBA behaviour"),
      (Anomalies
       | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where RuleStatus == "Production"
       | extend P = tolower(coalesce(iif(isempty(UserPrincipalName), '', UserPrincipalName),
                                     iif(isempty(UserName), '', UserName)))
       | where isnotempty(P) | where not(Scoped) or P in (InScope)
       | distinct P | extend Source = "UEBA anomaly"),
      (SecurityAlert
       | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where Entities has "account"
       | project Entities
       | mv-expand E = todynamic(Entities)
       | where tostring(E.Type) =~ "account"
       | extend AcctName = tostring(E.Name), Sfx = tostring(E.UPNSuffix)
       | where isnotempty(AcctName)
       | extend P = tolower(iif(isnotempty(Sfx), strcat(AcctName, "@", Sfx), AcctName))
       | where not(Scoped) or P in (InScope)
       | distinct P | extend Source = "Analytics alert")
    | lookup kind=leftouter (Ident | project P = tolower(AccountUPN), Department) on P
    | extend Department = iif(isempty(Department), "Unmapped", Department)
    | summarize Count = dcount(P) by Segment = Department, Source
    | extend Detail = Source,
             Note   = "A user appearing under more than one source is corroborated -- that is the high-signal case."
    | where Sel == "Users with risk signal";
//
let B_Dept =
    Ident
    | where Sel == "Departments mapped"
    | summarize Count = dcount(AccountObjectId),
                WithTitle = dcountif(AccountObjectId, isnotempty(JobTitle))
        by Segment = Department
    | extend Detail = strcat(tostring(WithTitle), " with a job title"),
             Note   = "Unmapped means IdentityInfo.Department is empty -- an Entra attribute gap, not a security finding."
    | project Segment, Detail, Count, Note;
//
let B_Inc =
    SecurityIncident
    | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
    | where Status != "Closed"
    | where Sel == "Open incidents"
    | summarize Count = count() by Segment = Severity, Status
    | extend Detail = Status,
             Note   = "Severity is the rule author's view. It is one input to the incident priority score, not the whole of it.";
//
union isfuzzy=true
    (B_Total   | project Segment, Detail, Count, Note),
    (B_Enabled | project Segment, Detail, Count, Note),
    (B_Priv    | project Segment, Detail, Count, Note),
    (B_Risk    | project Segment, Detail, Count, Note),
    (B_Dept    | project Segment, Detail, Count, Note),
    (B_Inc     | project Segment, Detail, Count, Note)
| extend Total = toscalar(
      union isfuzzy=true
        (B_Total | summarize sum(Count)), (B_Enabled | summarize sum(Count)),
        (B_Priv  | summarize sum(Count)), (B_Risk    | summarize sum(Count)),
        (B_Dept  | summarize sum(Count)), (B_Inc     | summarize sum(Count))
      | summarize sum(sum_Count))
| extend SharePct = iif(Total > 0, round(100.0 * Count / Total, 1), 0.0)
| project Segment, Detail, Count, SharePct, Note
| order by Count desc

content.query:
// Right panel of the privileged drill-down. Populates when a row is selected on
// the left; shows the actual identities behind that Division x Role cell.
//
// Selection is exported as a single composite key ("Division||Role") rather than
// two separate exported parameters. One exported field is the shape confirmed
// working in Microsoft's own published workbooks; splitting a composite here
// avoids depending on the multi-export schema.
let Key      = "{SelectedPrivRow}";
let Division = tostring(split(Key, "||")[0]);
let Role     = tostring(split(Key, "||")[1]);
let Ident = materialize(
    IdentityInfo
    | project TimeGenerated, AccountObjectId, AccountUPN, AccountDisplayName,
              Department, JobTitle, AssignedRoles, IsAccountEnabled, City, Country
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by AccountObjectId
    | extend Dept = iif(isempty(Department), "Unmapped", Department));
let Members =
    Ident
    | where Dept =~ Division
    | mv-expand RoleRaw = todynamic(AssignedRoles)
    | extend RoleName = coalesce(tostring(RoleRaw.Name),
                                 tostring(RoleRaw.roleName),
                                 tostring(RoleRaw.DisplayName),
                                 tostring(RoleRaw))
    | where RoleName =~ Role
    | extend Principal = tolower(AccountUPN)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by AccountObjectId
    | extend TotalRoles = array_length(todynamic(AssignedRoles));
// Risk context, so the panel answers "should I care about these people"
// rather than only "who are they".
let RiskySignals =
    union isfuzzy=true
      (BehaviorAnalytics
       | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where InvestigationPriority > 0
       | extend P = tolower(coalesce(iif(isempty(UserPrincipalName), '', UserPrincipalName),
                                     iif(isempty(ActorPrincipalName), '', ActorPrincipalName),
                                     iif(isempty(UserName), '', UserName)))
       | where isnotempty(P)
       | summarize Score = sum(InvestigationPriority), Kind = "UEBA" by P),
      (Anomalies
       | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where RuleStatus == "Production"
       | extend P = tolower(coalesce(iif(isempty(UserPrincipalName), '', UserPrincipalName),
                                     iif(isempty(UserName), '', UserName)))
       | where isnotempty(P)
       | summarize Score = tolong(round(sum(Score) * 10)), Kind = "Anomaly" by P)
    | summarize RiskSignal = sum(Score), Sources = make_set(Kind, 5) by P;
Members
| extend Principal = tolower(AccountUPN)
| lookup kind=leftouter RiskySignals on $left.Principal == $right.P
| extend RiskSignal = coalesce(RiskSignal, tolong(0))
| extend Subject = iif("{Identify}" == "Named",
                       iif(isempty(AccountDisplayName), Principal, AccountDisplayName),
                       strcat("ANON-", toupper(substring(hash_sha256(Principal), 0, 6))))
| extend Account = iif("{Identify}" == "Named", Principal, "(pseudonymised)")
| extend Standing = case(IsAccountEnabled == false, "Disabled",
                         TotalRoles >= 5,           "Enabled / 5+ roles",
                         TotalRoles >= 3,           "Enabled / 3-4 roles",
                                                    "Enabled")
| extend Flag = case(IsAccountEnabled == false and TotalRoles > 0, "Disabled but still role-bearing",
                     RiskSignal > 0,                               "Has risk signal in window",
                     TotalRoles >= 5,                              "Broad standing privilege",
                                                                   "")
| project Subject, Account, JobTitle, Standing, TotalRoles, RiskSignal, Flag,
          Location = strcat(iif(isempty(City), "-", City), iif(isempty(Country), "", strcat(", ", Country)))
| order by RiskSignal desc, TotalRoles desc
| take 200

content.json:
Data readiness
What is actually feeding the numbers above. Amber or red here explains any empty panel below — check it before drawing conclusions. Tenant-wide by design, so it stays honest under any filter.
Signal sources  The six tables the model reads. A source at zero is a plumbing finding, not a security finding.

content.query:
// Data readiness -- signal sources, rendered as tiles.
// Split from the field-coverage panel so each renders as a clean 6-tile row
// rather than a grouped grid crammed into a scroll box.
union isfuzzy=true
  (IdentityInfo      | summarize Rows = tolong(count()), Latest = max(TimeGenerated)
                     | extend Rank = 1, Signal = "IdentityInfo",      Needed = "Headcount, division, manager"),
  (BehaviorAnalytics | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | summarize Rows = tolong(count()), Latest = max(TimeGenerated)
                     | extend Rank = 2, Signal = "BehaviorAnalytics", Needed = "Investigation Priority"),
  (Anomalies         | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | summarize Rows = tolong(count()), Latest = max(TimeGenerated)
                     | extend Rank = 3, Signal = "Anomalies",         Needed = "Anomaly score, MITRE tactics"),
  (SecurityAlert     | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | summarize Rows = tolong(count()), Latest = max(TimeGenerated)
                     | extend Rank = 4, Signal = "SecurityAlert",     Needed = "Alerts by division"),
  (SecurityIncident  | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | summarize Rows = tolong(count()), Latest = max(TimeGenerated)
                     | extend Rank = 5, Signal = "SecurityIncident",  Needed = "Incident context"),
  (UserPeerAnalytics | summarize Rows = tolong(count()), Latest = max(TimeGenerated)
                     | extend Rank = 6, Signal = "UserPeerAnalytics", Needed = "Peer comparison")
// Coverage is a readiness signal, not a percentage of anything real: a source is
// either feeding the model or it is not. Three states keeps the tile honest.
| extend Coverage = case(Rows > 1000, 100, Rows > 0, 55, 0)
| extend Status   = case(Rows > 1000, "Ready", Rows > 0, "Thin", "No data")
| extend Age = iif(isnull(Latest), "never",
                   case(Latest > ago(1h),  "just now",
                        Latest > ago(24h), strcat(tostring(toint(datetime_diff('hour', now(), Latest))), "h ago"),
                                           strcat(tostring(toint(datetime_diff('day', now(), Latest))), "d ago")))
| extend StatusLine = strcat(Status, "  ·  ", iif(Rows > 0, strcat(tostring(Rows), " rows  ·  ", Age), "nothing ingested"))

content.query:
// Data readiness -- IdentityInfo field coverage, rendered as tiles.
// This is the panel that predicts whether the division-level requirement can be
// met at all: if Department is red here, every by-division panel says "Unmapped".
let Ident = materialize(
    IdentityInfo
    | project TimeGenerated, AccountObjectId, Department, JobTitle, Manager,
              BlastRadius, MailAddress, AssignedRoles
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by AccountObjectId);
let Total = toscalar(Ident | count);
Ident
| summarize Department      = countif(isnotempty(Department)),
            JobTitle        = countif(isnotempty(JobTitle)),
            Manager         = countif(isnotempty(Manager)),
            BlastRadius     = countif(isnotempty(tostring(BlastRadius))),
            MailAddress     = countif(isnotempty(MailAddress)),
            DirectoryRoles  = countif(array_length(todynamic(AssignedRoles)) > 0)
| extend Bag = pack("Department", Department, "Job title", JobTitle,
                    "Manager", Manager, "Blast radius", BlastRadius,
                    "Mail address", MailAddress, "Directory roles", DirectoryRoles)
| mv-expand Bag
| extend Signal    = tostring(bag_keys(Bag)[0]),
         Populated = tolong(Bag[tostring(bag_keys(Bag)[0])])
| extend Coverage = iif(Total > 0, toint(round(100.0 * Populated / Total)), 0)
| extend Status   = case(Coverage >= 80, "Ready", Coverage >= 20, "Partial", "No data")
// KQL has no format_number(); thousands separators are not worth a custom
// implementation on a status line.
| extend StatusLine = strcat(Status, "  ·  ", tostring(Populated),
                             " of ", tostring(Total), " identities")
| extend Needed = case(
      Signal == "Department",      "Division breakdown -- requirement 3",
      Signal == "Job title",       "Context on the elevated-risk list",
      Signal == "Manager",         "Manager verification playbook",
      Signal == "Blast radius",    "Impact axis of the risk index",
      Signal == "Mail address",    "Notification and identity resolution",

| extend Rank = case(Signal == "Department", 1, Signal == "Blast radius", 2,
                     Signal == "Directory roles", 3, Signal == "Manager", 4,

ⓘ  Severity is an input to the priority score, not a rival to it
A Medium at 98 and a High at 28 is not a contradiction. The two numbers answer different questions.
A **Medium** incident scoring **98** and a **High** incident scoring **28** is not a contradiction, and it is not a bug. The two numbers answer different questions: | | Set by | Question it answers | Scope | |---|---|---|---| | **Severity** | the rule author, when the detection was written | *How bad is this **class** of thing, in general?* | static, same in every tenant | | **Priority score** | the Defender Queue Assistant model, per incident | *How much should **you** work **this one**, **now**, in **your** environment?* | dynamic, tenant-specific | Severity is **one of roughly eleven documented inputs** to the priority score. So a Medium at 98 simply means the other ten inputs outweighed the severity term. A High at 28 means the opposite — the severity term was the only thing it had going for it.
The two explanations that cover almost every case
**Why a Medium climbs.** Critical assets involved · several MITRE techniques chained rather than one · a rare alert type · attack-disruption fired · a threat-analytics match on an active campaign · high blast-radius or privileged identities in scope. **Why a High falls.** The rule is authored High but fires constantly in *your* tenant · it has a poor confirmed-true-positive record here · a single alert, single technique, no chain · no critical assets · common technique the model sees everywhere. That second one is the important half, and it is the one people find counter-intuitive: **the model discounts detections that have a bad track record in your environment.** A High-severity rule with a 70% false-positive rate is, empirically, a low-priority rule — whatever its author intended.
ⓘ  How to answer the question in a meeting
Do not try to recompute the score. Put both incidents' documented factors side by side and let the evidence carry the explanation.
Microsoft does **not** publish the weights, so nobody can recompute the score. Do not try. Instead do the thing that is actually defensible: put both incidents' documented factors side by side and let the evidence carry the explanation. Enter two incident numbers in **Incident A** and **Incident B** above. The table below measures every factor Microsoft lists as an input, on both incidents, and states which way each one pushes. The sentence you are aiming for is: > "The Medium outranked the High because it touched three critical assets across four MITRE techniques from two products, and involved two privileged identities. The High was a single alert from a rule that fired 4,200 times in ninety days and was closed as a false positive 71% of the time." That is an explanation a regulator, an auditor and a sceptical analyst will all accept — and none of it depends on knowing the model's coefficients.
ⓘ  Note on the noise metrics
Read this before quoting columns 13 to 16.
Microsoft lists **"alert types and rarity"** and **"SnR"** as inputs but never defines them numerically. Columns 13–16 are therefore **your own measured proxies**, computed from your own ninety-day history — not Microsoft's internal values. They are presented as *evidence that explains the ranking*, not as a claim about what the model calculated. That distinction matters if this ever ends up in front of an auditor. The false-positive rate is only as good as your closure hygiene. If analysts close incidents as *Undetermined*, this column is blind — which is its own finding, and a cheap one to fix.

content.json: **If you disagree with a ranking, these are the levers — in order of effect.** 1) Populate **Critical Asset Management**; asset criticality is a documented first-class input and is pure configuration. 2) Fix the **authored severity** on rules that are chronically wrong. 3) Close incidents with an accurate **classification and reason** — an Undetermined queue teaches nobody anything and blinds your own noise metrics. 4) Retire or tune rules with a false-positive rate above roughly 50%; they are diluting every incident they touch.

Three different things are called "score"
They are not comparable with each other. Mixing them up is the single most common source of confusion in a UEBA deployment.
| | Where it lives | Scale | Granularity | What it actually measures | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Investigation Priority** | `BehaviorAnalytics.InvestigationPriority`, entity pages | **0–10** integer | **Per event** | How far a single activity deviates from the user's own baseline, their peer group's baseline, and the tenant baseline | | **Incident priority score** | Defender portal incident queue and review panel; Graph `security/incidents` → `priorityScore` | **0–100** integer | **Per incident** | ML ranking of which incident deserves attention first | | **Anomaly score** | `Anomalies.Score` | **0–1** float | **Per anomaly** | Degree of deviation for that specific anomaly rule |
ⓘ  The direct answer: these scores measure quality, not quantity
More assets, more alerts and more users do not mechanically raise them.
More assets, more alerts and more users **do not mechanically raise** either the Investigation Priority or the incident priority score. - **Investigation Priority** is a *per-event novelty* measure. One user doing one thing they have never done before, from a country the tenant has never seen, on a dormant account with a high blast radius, can score **9–10**. Ten users each doing fifty entirely normal things score **1–2 per event** — many events, still low. - **Incident priority score** rises with *threat quality*: severity, attack-disruption signals, threat analytics, MITRE techniques, **asset criticality**, alert rarity, and high-profile threat classes such as ransomware. Ten medium alerts on ordinary assets will typically rank **below** one high-severity alert on an asset tagged *Very High* criticality. So the honest framing is: **a bigger incident is not automatically a more urgent one.** Volume tells you about scope; these scores tell you about likelihood and consequence.
What Microsoft publishes, and what it does not
**Published.** The 0–10 scale and its meaning. That Investigation Priority combines an *Entity Anomaly Score* (rarity of user / device / country) with a *Time Series Score* (spikes over 5–7 day windows). The full catalogue of ~35 boolean enrichment flags in `ActivityInsights` and their individual lookback windows, which range from 5 to 180 days. That `BlastRadius` is derived from org-tree position plus Entra roles. That peer groups are built with TF-IDF over directory membership, ranked to the top 20 peers, with smaller groups weighted more heavily. For the incident score, the factor list and the colour bands: red above 85, orange 15–85, grey below 15. **Not published.** The coefficients. Microsoft does not state how the two sub-scores are weighted against each other, what a `BlastRadius` of High is worth numerically, or how the 10-plus incident factors are combined. There is no published score distribution, so there is no vendor-defined answer to "what counts as high in our tenant". **Two things worth knowing.** First, Microsoft's own analytics-rule templates threshold Investigation Priority at `> 0` rather than at a band — which suggests the scale is built for *ranking*, not for threshold rules. Second, `IdentityInfo` carries `InvestigationPriority` and `InvestigationPriorityPercentile` columns that Microsoft explicitly documents as **not used or supported**. They exist in the schema and are empty. Anything built on them silently returns nothing.
ⓘ  Which is why this dashboard scores separately
Because the vendor weights are unpublished, this workbook does not try to reverse-engineer them.
Because the vendor weights are not published, this workbook does **not** try to reverse-engineer them. It computes its own composite index that is fully transparent, and shows the Microsoft scores as inputs alongside it. | Component | Axis | Cap | Source | |---|---|---|---| | UEBA behaviour priority | Quality | 25 | `BehaviorAnalytics` — cumulative Investigation Priority ÷ 4 | | UEBA anomalies | Quality | 20 | `Anomalies` — summed `Score` × 4 | | Kill-chain breadth | Quality | 20 | distinct MITRE tactics, `(n − 1) × 7` | | Analytics-rule alerts | **Volume** | 25 | `SecurityAlert` severity-weighted: High 10, Medium 5, Low 2, Info 1 | | Blast radius / privilege | Impact | 10 | `IdentityInfo.BlastRadius` + directory role count | Two design choices matter. **Breadth uses `(n − 1)`, so a single tactic scores zero.** One chatty rule can dominate volume; it cannot fake breadth. That is what stops a noisy detection from manufacturing a critical-looking user. **Quality, Volume and Impact stay visible as separate columns.** Two people can both score 60 and mean entirely different things — one from behavioural novelty across four tactics, the other from a single rule firing forty times. Blending them into one number hides exactly the distinction an analyst needs. Every weight lives in one block at the top of each query, labelled `RISK MODEL`. Change a cap there and every panel moves together.
Your own distribution
Microsoft does not publish one. This is measured from your tenant, which makes it the only defensible basis for choosing a threshold.
